html:
Typee is the first book of the American writer Herman Melville, published in 1846. It tells of the weeks he spent in the Taipivai valley of Nuku Hiva, in the Marquesas, after deserting a whaling ship in 1842.

The book was a best seller. It praised the Marquesans' life while dwelling on fears of cannibalism, and criticised missionaries and the French, who had just taken the islands.

Typee set the pattern of Western writing about Polynesia as a lost paradise, followed by Stevenson and by the painter Gauguin, who died in the Marquesas in 1903. Disease meanwhile killed most Marquesans in the 19th century.
